subject: Re: [AMBER] Issue heating system in equilibration step

messages.author: Samuel A. Ratliff
messages.body:
I fiddled around with my .in file and modified the 02_Heat.in file on the AMBER lipid tutorial page. I'll include it below in case other people run into the same issue down the road. I'm still having issues with my system, but it's related to a bond made by tleap and I'll start a new thread for that.
Sam
Lipid 128 heating 100K
&cntrl
imin=0,         ! Molecular dynamics
ntx=1,          ! Positions read formatted with no initial velocities
irest=0,        ! No restart
ntc=2,          ! SHAKE on for bonds with hydrogen
ntf=2,          ! No force evaluation for bonds with hydrogen
tol=0.0000001,  ! SHAKE tolerance
nstlim=25000,    ! Number of MD steps
ntt=3,          ! Langevin thermostat
gamma_ln=1.0,   ! Collision frequency for Langevin thermostat IS 5 in ours
ntr=1,          ! Restrain atoms using a harmonic potential
! (See the GROUP input below)
ig=-1,          ! Random seed for Langevin thermostat
ntpr=100,
ntwr=10000,
ntwx=100,       ! Write to trajectory file every ntwx steps
dt=0.002,       ! Timestep (ps)
nmropt=1,       ! NMR restraints will be read (See TEMP0 control below)
ntb=1,
ntp=0,
cut=10.0,
ioutfm=1,       ! Write a binary (netcdf) trajectory
ntxo=2,         ! Write binary restart files
restraintmask=':1-1215', ! Restrain the lipids and the protein
restraint_wt=4.0,
&end
&wt
type='TEMP0',   ! Varies the target temperature TEMP0
istep1=0,       ! Initial step
istep2=25000,    ! Final step
value1=0.0,     ! Initial temp0 (K)
value2=310.0 /  ! final temp0 (K)
&wt type='END' / ! End of varying conditions
________________________________________
From: Samuel A. Ratliff
Sent: Friday, July 31, 2020 4:14 PM
To: AMBER Mailing List
Subject: Re: [AMBER] Issue heating system in equilibration step
Will give that a go, thanks.
Sam

have you tried the same inputs on the CPU version?
I suggest continuing to simplify the inputs stepswise (no restraints, no
weight changes, no nmropt restraints) and see if you can get it to work,
the focus on the variable that made the difference .

> next section of the output. Otherwise, the results are identical.
